old_findings.note: Still 21 'revert with memory from mem[64]' custom-error reverts.

improvements: unknown529dca32: the bytes length read back from memory (mem[_24]) is forwarded as _23, and its 0xe7c8d4cf revert is decoded with its bytes argument split into length and data (6 lines -> 1); hex constants show whole bytes (0x01.., 9 lines).
notes: Diff of 293 lines; no effect differs (calls, events, writes, reverts identical in count). In unknown529dca32 the held free-pointer bases (_24, _27, _56 = mem[64]) are now spelled as sums (_21 + ceil32(_20) + ceil32(_23) + 96...), which lengthens some address lines while the forwarded lengths shorten others; the text size is unchanged (223 KB), so I count it as neutral here.
summary: No regression; small gains in unknown529dca32 (forwarded length, decoded error) and the hex display; round 1's memory reverts remain.
